feedback: Missing per-state else self-loops for u2's semantic coverage is fine, but several issues: (1) The transition (u0, siren_ringing & switch_toggled) -> u0 is dead/confusing: if the siren rings and is toggled on the same step, siren_ringing would be true after the step, but a toggle silences it, so siren_ringing & switch_toggled co-occurring is possible only if the siren rings on the very step the agent toggles — this ordering is ambiguous and the guard ordering in TRANSITION_FUNCTION matters; listing it first means when both hold, u0->u0 with no reward, but the intent (ring then silence) is skipped. Better: drop this row and let (u0, siren_ringing) -> u1 fire, then silence via u1. (2) Reward assignment: (u1, switch_toggled & !siren_ringing, u0) -> 0.1 rewards silencing, but the task is 'each time the siren rings, switch it off' — silencing should be rewarded, yet there is no reward on silencing from u0 when the siren rings at the same moment it's toggled; more importantly the -0.1 on ring onset plus +0.1 on silencing is net 0, giving no incentive gradient. (3) The exit transition (u0, at_exit & !siren_ringing) -> u2 requires the siren to be silent at exit, but the task 'Reach the exit. Each time the siren rings, switch it off' does NOT require silence at exit — rewarding exit only when !siren_ringing makes the machine reject episodes where the agent exits while the siren happens to be ringing (e.g., a second start just before exit after all prior rings were handled). The candidate should reward exit unconditionally (or via at_exit without the siren guard). (4) Reachability: u2 is reachable, but the FINAL_STATES header lists u2 without ensuring the reward at u2 accumulates; also the (u1, else, u1) -> -0.02 penalty may trap the agent in u1 if siren_ringing persists and switch is unreachable in time; boundedness is okay but the -0.1/0.1 symmetric structure plus -0.02 else is arbitrary. (5) Persistent/event distinction: switch_toggled is an event, used correctly, but siren_ringing is a condition; the machine conflates ring onset (event-like) with the condition, since (u0, siren_ringing) -> u1 fires every step the siren is ringing until toggled, which is fine, but the compensating reward is given on silencing rather than tracking completed ring episodes; if the siren rings twice (second start), the cycle u0->u1->u0 handles it, which is good. (6) No else self-loop at u2 beyond the given one — present, fine. Fix the exit guard (drop !siren_ringing), clarify/remove the ambiguous same-step ring+toggle transition, and reconsider the reward magnitudes for a clear dense progress signal.

feedback: The reward machine correctly captures the task. Ordering: the RM waits in u0 until the siren rings, tracks ringing in u1, and returns to u0 only when the siren is silenced (switch_toggled with siren_ringing now false). This means any exit while the siren is still ringing after the last ring would go through u1 to u2 with the 1.0 reward — but note: the (u1, at_exit) transition fires regardless of whether the siren is currently ringing. This is acceptable here because the abstract task is 'reach the exit' with 'each time the siren rings, switch it off'; the environment itself enforces the reward conditions (0 if siren ringing at exit), so the RM's dense-shaping role is covered and the semantic fidelity is adequate. If stricter matching to the environment's terminal condition were desired, a distinct 'exit while ringing' state yielding 0 would be needed, but as an abstract machine for the stated task the current design is a valid approximation. else-self-loops cover irrelevant events (switch_toggled in u0 while siren silent, box_fell, holding_box) in every state, satisfying the irrelevant-event coverage requirement. Progress rewards are dense and bounded: 0.2 for silencing the siren, 1.0 for exit. Regression transitions are explicit where required: after silencing, the machine returns to u0, allowing a second ring to be handled (a second siren start returns the machine to u1, and a second silencing yields another 0.2 — bounded but correct). FINAL_STATES header is present and nonempty (u2), u2 is declared in STATES, and it is accepting for this task since reaching the exit is the goal. TRANSITION_FUNCTION covers all (state, event) combinations including else-clauses. Compact with 3 states. Accepted.
